# HarnessDock v0.2.2

v0.2.2 makes the Tauri product line explicitly **Full-only** and fixes branding/install regressions found by inspecting the actual candidate binaries.

## Installation and branding

- Windows, Linux and macOS public desktop packages include the pinned local dsh runtime. No Thin installer is published. The retained Electron Thin implementation remains source-only for compatibility and can be removed after the Full-only line has proven stable.
- Windows NSIS installer and uninstaller now explicitly use the HarnessDock icon. The previous v0.2.1 installer was verified to contain the default NSIS blue-arrow icon even though the application bundle icon was configured.
- Windows installer header/sidebar branding is generated from the same HarnessDock source artwork.
- Candidate CI parses the final Windows PE icon resources and compares them with the HarnessDock ICO, preventing a future silent fallback to NSIS defaults.
- Android and iOS native projects regenerate their launcher/app icon sets from the 1024x1024 HarnessDock source after `tauri android/ios init`. Android CI also verifies the generated launcher hash changes from the Tauri template default.

## Upgrade experience

- The application identifier remains `com.harnessdock.client`, preserving the v0.2.x app identity and data location for in-place upgrades.
- Windows remains current-user installation to avoid unnecessary elevation/UAC prompts.
- Accidental downgrade installation is blocked.
- The WebView2 bootstrapper is embedded in the Windows installer, reducing a network dependency during installer startup while still allowing WebView2 to be installed when missing.
- Full packages keep the pinned runtime local, so first launch does not require a separate dsh runtime download.

## Resilience

- The plugin fault-containment improvements remain enabled: third-party plugin failures trigger bounded recovery/quarantine rather than terminating HarnessDock.
- Official `@deepseek-ai/*` components and the HarnessDock embedded-client bridge are never automatically quarantined.
- Recovered sessions are reported as degraded with isolated/suspected plugin diagnostics and an expiring quarantine record.
- Desktop startup now opens the isolated official Harness Web UI automatically. The local Runtime/Gateway control page is hidden during normal startup and is shown only when a fatal startup problem needs user action.
- Windows release binaries use the GUI subsystem and `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` for bundled Node/sidecar processes, so starting HarnessDock does not open a CMD window.
- If a user/plugin layer prevents normal recovery, the host retries with a temporary clean DSH profile. The user's real DSH configuration is not modified, and the Web UI remains available in safe mode.

## Verification

Publication requires both normal CI and the complete Full-only Tauri candidate to succeed for the exact current main SHA. The matrix covers Windows NSIS, Linux deb/AppImage, macOS x64/arm64 DMG, four pinned Runtime bundles, Android APK/AAB, iOS Simulator archive, Runtime smoke tests, plugin recovery tests, icon-generation guards and the Windows installer icon binary check.

- macOS release DMGs are assembled from the validated Tauri `.app` plus an `/Applications` drag target using a mount-free `hdiutil -srcfolder` path, avoiding the repeatable DiskArbitration detach timeout seen on GitHub Intel runners.
- Release automation now distinguishes a genuinely missing tag/release from an API error payload before choosing create versus replace, preventing a missing `v0.2.2` tag from being mistaken for an existing ref.

Public CI artifacts remain unsigned developer builds (no Windows Authenticode, Apple notarization, production Android signing or App Store/TestFlight provisioning). Release assets include `SHA256SUMS`.
